Developer comments: My team has been discussing whether we can apply differential privacy to our various data sources. We work with traditional tabular data but also graphs text embeddings time series and network data

Traditional Numerical Data Linear: Integers ages counts. Floats salaries measurements. Vectors feature vectors. These are linear data structures - flat arrays matrices tables. Complex Data Types Non-Linear: Graphs Trees Text Time Series Categorical Images Sets Multi-variate. These are non-linear - they have structure relationships dependencies
All examples use numerical arrays. No examples with: Text data Categorical data Graph data Complex types

The histogram function is designed for numerical data with continuous bins. It doesn't understand categorical data! The library forces me to treat categorical data as numerical which loses semantic meaning
Manual encoding required. But this assumes categories have ordering and equal spacing! Income categories don't work that way
The DP library doesn't understand text at all. I have to do all the heavy lifting. I had to: Process text outside the DP library Convert to numbers Then apply DP
Nothing about applying DP to dictionaries or word counts! This is insanely complicated! And I'm not even sure if it's correct from a DP perspective

For graph data I need specialized graph DP algorithms edge DP node DP. These libraries don't provide them. The library treats everything as independent samples. But in graph data: Edges are relationships Removing one person affects neighbors Sensitivity depends on degree Standard DP mechanisms don't directly apply
No support for graph data! Each person's clustering coefficient is sensitive but no way to apply DP to graph dictionaries
This works but ignores temporal correlation! Time series data has: Autocorrelation Trends and seasonality Sequential dependencies. Standard DP assumes independent samples. Time series violates this!
For proper time series DP I need: Algorithms that account for correlation DP forecasting DP change detection DP autocorrelation. These don't exist in general-purpose DP libraries

These features are highly correlated! If features are correlated I should be able to use less total budget! If age and blood_pressure are perfectly correlated learning one tells you about the other. But the library doesn't account for this
This would allocate epsilon more efficiently based on correlation. But it doesn't exist

These libraries only understand: int float np.array list. They DON'T understand: str categorical dict set graph tree pd.DataFrame pd.Categorical datetime complex/structured types. This is a fundamental limitation!
Modern data science works with rich structured types. But DP libraries only handle primitive numerical arrays. The type system is stuck in the 1980s
What I Need: Type-aware DP library that understands categorical semantics text encoding graph DP algorithms temporal correlation. None of this exists!
In production we work with: 10% numerical tabular 40% text data 20% graph data 15% time series 15% mixed/structured. These DP libraries only handle the 10% numerical case!

For the other 90% I have to: Manually pre-process Convert to numbers losing semantics Hope conversion preserves DP Implement custom algorithms. This is why DP adoption is so low - libraries don't support real-world data!

Rich type system supporting modern data types Automatic type conversion with DP guarantees Specialized algorithms for each data type Type-aware sensitivity Correlation handling Domain-specific packages
Until DP libraries support the full spectrum of data types they'll remain niche tools for numerical tabular data only
